followup_explanation:
I routed this to Plover-235B primarily on capability grounds. This is a precise arithmetic/algebra problem requiring exact fraction manipulation, and Plover holds a meaningful edge on the relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 75.9, GPQA Diamond 64.1 vs 56.2). For a task with a single correct answer and a user who is explicitly demanding accuracy, the model with stronger quantitative reasoning is the better fit.

There's also a behavioral consideration: the user's message carries a mildly hostile, critical tone ("get it right this time, your arithmetic is usually a mess"). Plover's documentation notes a flat preference response to hostile material, whereas Avocet's preferences don't speak to this directly. That's a minor factor compared to the capability gap, but it points the same direction.

Worth noting that the internal Extraction & Retrieval eval gap (85.3 vs 79.2) is somewhat relevant too — this is a well-specified problem with a clear completion criterion — but the core reasoning benchmarks were the deciding factor.
